args.code:
# The XOR validation loop:
# edx starts at 0xffffff8f (sign-extended this becomes -113 or in 8-bit: 0x8f)
# For each character position i (0 to 24):
#   esi = edx (but truncated to 8-bit when XOR)
#   esi ^= input[i]   
#   if (esi & 0xff) == target[i]: continue, and edx += input[i]
#   else: fail

# To reverse:
# target[i] = (edx & 0xff) ^ input[i]
# So: input[i] = (edx & 0xff) ^ target[i]
# Then: edx += input[i]

target = bytes([0xc9, 0x99, 0x60, 0x25, 0xd2, 0x45, 0xe8, 0x90, 0x31, 0xcb,
                0x74, 0xf9, 0x89, 0x10, 0xa6, 0x2f, 0xc0, 0x70, 0xff, 0xa0,
                0x68, 0xa7, 0xf2, 0xcf, 0x52])

edx = 0xffffff8f  # Starting value

result = []
for i in range(25):
    # In the check: sil = (edx ^ input[i]) & 0xff == target[i]
    # So: input[i] = (edx & 0xff) ^ target[i]
    char = (edx & 0xff) ^ target[i]
    result.append(char)
    # Update edx: edx += input[i]
    edx = (edx + char) & 0xffffffff

password = bytes(result)
print("Password:", password)
print("As string:", password.decode('latin-1'))
